#1290. Man Utd Appointing Mauricio Pochettino is Bad News for 4 Stars

Mauricio Pochettino has been chasing the Manchester United job since 2019, and it seems as though he could finally be about to land it.

GIVEMESPORT sources understand that manager Michael Carrick is set to be relieved of his duties after a poor start to the season which has left Man Utd 18th in the Premier League table, with just one win from their opening ten games.

Former Spurs and Chelsea boss Pochettino is believed to be one of the top contenders, with his new contract with the USMNT, which runs until 2030, containing a $10m (£7.4m) release clause that can be triggered to get him in immediately, while it's also understood that he is very keen on the job.

Should he get the job and come in during the international break, his first game in charge will be one to remember: a trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool.

He will have the break to come in and start to implement his philosophies and style of play on the players that are not with their nations, which will include the likes of Joshua Zirkzee and Kobbie Mainoo.

But while some players will likely benefit hugely from his arrival and the way he wants to play, four in particular will suffer because they simply don't fit what he likes in his teams.

Harry Maguire has had a weird Manchester United career since joining the club from Leicester in an £80m deal.

He wore the captain's armband, got dropped, struggled for form, scored hugely important goals, and has now won his place back. But his form this season has been poor, and physically he has never been the most athletic. That's something that Pochettino likes in his defenders, and with the 33-year-old out of contract at the end of the season, it would be a surprise to see him kept around.

Considering Matthijs De Ligt, Lisandro Martinez, Leny Yoro, and Ayden Heaven are all in the squad and suit the type of profile Pochettino would prefer to have, this could be the beginning of the end for Maguire at Old Trafford.

The Morocco international was a shrewd signing when he joined from Bayern Munich in a deal worth over £17m, and he has been a good servant at left-back, right-back, and even in central defence during his time at the club.

Known more for his defensive security than his attacking prowess, Pochettino is known to like full-backs who can get up and down the pitch and be of use further up the pitch. Diogo Dalot's profile suits that much more than Mazraoui's, and that means the former Ajax star could find himself as a firm back-up option under the Argentine's management.

His current contract is due to expire in 2028, with the option for a further 12 months, but it wouldn't be a shock to see him on the move in 2027 if he isn't playing regularly.

Luke Shaw made his breakthrough as a teenager at Southampton under Pochettino, and they got on like a house on fire. Man Utd snapped Shaw up in a £31m deal, making him one of the world's most expensive teens at the time, and he has gone on to have a long career at Old Trafford.

But now 31 and out of contract at the end of the season, it's clear that Shaw shouldn't have a long-term future at the club. As mentioned, Pochettino likes athletic full-backs who can get up and down the pitch, and Shaw's fitness problems mean he simply can't do that anymore.

His injury concerns have already seen him miss a host of games this season too, and with Patrick Dorgu being able to take the role and perform as Pochettino likes, and a new left-back expected to arrive in 2027, Shaw's time at the club looks set to be coming to an end.

When Mount joined in a £60m deal from Chelsea, there were many fans questioning what the point of the deal was. Now into his fourth season, Mount is still yet to rack up a 10 goal contributions with the club, and his injuries continue to be an issue.

Pochettino may be a fan of his style of play. He is technically tidy, has a decent engine, and tends to make good decisions on the ball. But the 54-year-old prioritises fitness and ensures his teams are able to run for a full 90 minutes so they can compete at the highest level. That will put a lot of pressure on Mount, and based on previous evidence, his body would not be able to cope.

More injuries would surely see the board consider cutting their losses, and if he can't stay fit then Pochettino is unlikely to stand in the way of an exit.

#1289. Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

“Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”

Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and said: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg

For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he said. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

Kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and said he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

For the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more important than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

Kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

There's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”

The plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before quickly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

#1288. Sources: Man Utd Finalising Deal to Appoint Mauricio Pochettino as Manager

Manchester United are finalising a deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, GIVEMESPORT sources understand. Although the club insist no final decision has been made on Michael Carrick's future yet, a Monaco meeting led by Sir Jim Ratcliffe is expected to recommend his departure. A board meeting is also scheduled for today likely to ratify the exit.

The Red Devils currently find themselves 18th in the Premier League table after a run of just one win in their opening 10 games this season, while Carrick has won just three of 15 games in all competitions since being handed a two-year deal to become permanent manager in the summer.

That run of form has seen Omar Berrada, and Jason Wilcox make the recommendation to part ways with Carrick.

GIVEMESPORT understands that Carrick is yet to be officially informed of the decision to sack him, and he is currently at Carrington due to take training on Wednesday morning as usual. However, Carrick could be informed as early as today.

Pochettino wants the job, having been linked with the role as long ago as 2019, and it's understood that terms are now being finalised for him to take over at Old Trafford.

The 54-year-old signed a new long-term contract with the USMNT after the 2026 World Cup, which would run until 2030. However, GMS understands that the deal contains a $10m (£7.4m) release clause, which United can trigger to get him in.

Pochettino is known to work with the same backroom staff wherever he goes, including his assistant Jesus Perez, and GIVEMESPORT understands that it would cost a further $2m (£1.5m) to bring them with him to Old Trafford. No formal contact has been made yet with US Soccer, but it's expected to be a straightforward process. The only challenge is the USA have two-legged Nations League quarter-final with Haiti during the international break.

GIVEMESPORT sources also understand that Carrick's contract at Man Utd contains a break clause that means compensation will be significantly less than previous Manchester United managers.

Pochettino, who has been described as 'world-class', is currently coaching the USMNT and took his team to the last sixteen of the 2026 World Cup, where they were defeated by Belgium.

The Argentine has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, and Chelsea in the Premier League, while he also reached the EFL Cup final twice and the Champions League final during his time with those clubs. He also won the Ligue 1 title with Paris Saint-Germain.

It sounds as if the big calls have already been made.

#1287. Como’s Ramon thanks Fabregas for Spain call-up

Jacobo Ramon has thanked Cesc Fabregas for his role in his first senior Spain call-up, saying Como’s decision to sign him from Real Madrid has been fully justified.

According to AS, via TuttoMercatoWeb, the 21-year-old centre-back found out about his first senior call-up from Luis de la Fuente through a message from Como teammate Assane Diao.

“Coming in here for the first time is a huge honour, and I’m really proud to be with the Selección,” Ramon said at Las Rozas before the squad left for Prague.

“I was at home and Assane Diao messaged me telling me to look at my phone. He sent me a photo of the list, and at first I couldn’t believe it.”

Ramon knew he was in Spain’s provisional squad but hadn’t spoken to the coach before the announcement.

“If I’m here, it’s thanks to the faith he’s shown in me and what I’m doing with Como. I want to keep going down this path,” he said.

The defender left Real Madrid for Como last summer, and he’s become a key part of Fabregas’ side. The Lariani are fourth in Serie A and made history with a record 9-1 win at Lens in the Champions League last week.

“I left Real Madrid to carve out a place for myself at the top level. I can’t say I’ve reached my goal, but I’m on the right path,” he said.

“Cesc believed in me straight away. He explained the project to me, and his way of seeing football suits my qualities perfectly. I’m really grateful to him.”

#1285. He Played 464 Games For Man Utd - But Depression Ruined His England Career

For many English football players, playing for the senior England national team is the pinnacle of your career.

Current captain Harry Kane is expected to become the most capped player of all-time when England take on Croatia on Thursday night at Wembley, where he will earn his 126th cap, surpassing Peter Shilton's 125 appearances for the Three Lions.

Just behind them is former captain and former all-time top scorer Wayne Rooney, who earned 121 caps in his senior career, who enjoyed a stunning individual career at club level during his time at Everton, Manchester United, and DC United.

While playing at Old Trafford in particular, Rooney played alongside a host of world-class talent, many of whom were English. Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand, Owen Hargreaves, and Paul Scholes all enjoyed brilliant careers at international level as well as with United, and they all absolutely loved their time with the Three Lions.

But someone else who played with those stars and represented the national team wasn't so keen, and has admitted that he was actually depressed during that time of his career.

Iconic midfielder Michael Carrick was considered to be one of the most underrated midfielders of his generation, because he barely got the nod at international level.

Carrick won 34 caps during his career, never scoring a goal, with just 22 of those appearances coming as a starter. But only 12 of those 34 appearances came in competitive games, with the rest coming in friendlies, showing that the managers rarely relied on him when it really mattered.

But speaking back in 2018, while still a player, Carrick revealed that part of the reason why he never earned more caps was because he asked for the FA to stop picking him as he felt depressed whenever he went away for camps.

“I’d been in the squad a long time and I’ll be honest, I was finding it hard going away with England. I didn’t mind going away with United pre-season for three weeks or whatever and coming back, but going with England, it was almost depressing in a way," he said.

“It made me really down, so I came to the point after South Africa where I thought: ‘I can’t do that again.’ People would be saying: ‘Pull yourself together and be grateful for it’ and I understood the position I was in, the privileged position I was in, but I just found it so hard, and I couldn’t deal with it anymore.

“I was probably on the verge of ... yes, I was depressed at times, yes. I told the FA: ‘Look, please don’t pick me.’”

Carrick was part of the England squad at the 2006 and 2010 World Cups, while he was on standby for the 2014 World Cup too. But he made just one appearance in a tournament, where he started in the 1-0 win over Ecuador in Stuttgart.

England's lack of success at tournaments was often put down to the failed partnership of Steven Gerrard and Frank Lampard in the centre of midfield, and with Carrick's reveal that he asked to be left out towards the end of his career, whether he could have been the difference maker will always remain one of the greatest what-ifs of that generation.

Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026

Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.

Pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley. But after an understandably tricky start in League One – two wins from their first 10 games – Woodman was shown the door.

In his first interview since that decision last month, the 55-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport about feelings of 'betrayal' and 'shock' before making his pitch to future employers. But the most eye-opening part of our candid conversation comes when I ask the man with more than four decades of experience to recall the club he took over in 2021.

‘Look, Bromley is your classic non-League club,’ says Woodman. ‘I mean that with the greatest respect to all non-League clubs and I hate the word “non-League” as I think it should be “League Three”, as they are all professional.

‘But the facilities are non-League, the mentality is non-League. Everything is done day-to-day, hand-to-mouth, every penny counts, every decision that costs money counts, it is run by people’s personal money.

‘It was tough when I started: we had no turnstiles, no club shop, we trained on the pitch because it was astroturf, we had no gym.’

Andy Woodman was sacked as Bromley boss last month despite leading the club to the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season

Woodman with the FA Trophy in 2022. 'Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair,' says the former Bromley boss

Under chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves, Woodman and Co, Bromley changed this mentality and shot up the pyramid, winning the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season. Two months later, it was all over.

Asked how he feels about the decision, Woodman, who used to coach in the Arsenal academy system, says: ‘Yeah, I feel betrayed. Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair. That’s fine, I get how the football business works.

‘But the bit that didn't sit comfortably with me was the conversations I was having with people at the club or owners, everyone above me… there was no inkling of any of this. I feel misled. I was surprised.

‘One day, we were talking about plans and the way forward and how to get through this sticky little period with players out injured, then the next minute it was a change of direction. Nothing like, “Right, you’ve got three games to turn it round”, none of that, nothing.

‘My record was good there, the owner always said if anyone can churn out results it was myself. Football has no patience. In football, people always forget where they come from. I understand wanting to move forward. It’s disappointing really, that’s the best word I can use. I feel let down.

‘It was just a normal day when they told me. I was going into training, popped across to where the chairman’s office was and then was just told, “We are going to take a change of direction”. It was no more than that, I didn’t try to change the decision or ask why.

‘It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is… I am sure people will read this and think, “You deserve this” and “You deserve that” but what else can you do? There’s no easy way of doing it.

'When you have been told you are sacked, you don’t really want to stick around and have a long conversation. They didn’t give an explanation. They needed results, they said. We lost to Leicester which was not a great result, obviously. But realistically they are Leicester… and we are Bromley.’

'It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is'

Woodman, who used to be the Arsenal youth team goalkeeping coach, says: 'When I left Bromley that day, I just felt in shock to be really honest'

To hammer home that last point: Woodman’s first game was against Wealdstone in April 2021 in the National League at Hayes Lane. On that same weekend, Leicester were hosting soon-to-be champions Manchester City. Oh, and the Foxes won the FA Cup a month later.

‘When I left that day, I just felt in shock to be honest,’ continues Woodman. ‘I felt the next three games were winnable. I had played seven of the top 10 teams, beaten the top team Huddersfield, my goalie was just coming back from injury and some others were coming back.

‘We had two teams in the bottom four and one just outside so I felt it was my best opportunity to get some much-needed results.

‘To take someone out who has been in football 40 years and been in coaching 25 years and then to put (his former assistant) Byron Webster in charge who had just been fresh out of playing and has never done a coaching session… with every respect, it feels unfair to him. It was a stupid thing to do. I found that really strange, they took one point from those three games. It fascinates me.’

Now, with Bromley bottom of League One, Karl Robinson, the former Salford and MK Dons boss, has taken over. Woodman, though, is keen not to sound bitter and will remember his five-and-a-half years at the club with fondness. He says his best memories are taking Bromley into the Football League, playing at Newcastle in the FA Cup and beating ‘Hollywood Netflix club Wrexham’ in the FA Trophy final.

Sir Gareth Southgate remains his best friend, the pair having met as teenagers in the Crystal Palace academy. They took turns in being best man at each other’s wedding and Southgate is godfather of goalkeeper Andy’s son Freddie, who is on Liverpool’s books.

They also co-authored the 2004 book Woody and Nord which chronicles two polar opposite career paths that started at the same level, one going on to play (and later manage) England, the other a journeyman in the lower leagues.

‘Nothing surprises Gareth and I,’ adds Woodman. ‘We have been in the game for 40 years now. You can argue that in his tenure at England, he got them as high as they have ever been in 60 years and it still was not enough. So it doesn’t surprise us. People have to make decisions and they are business-related, only time will tell if it is the right decision but that’s not my problem any more.

Woodman and lifelong friend Sir Gareth Southgate at the release of their 2004 book 'Woody and Nord' which charts two very different careers in football

Southgate is godfather to Woodman's son Freddie, a goalkeeper on Liverpool's books

‘Gareth was very supportive, so was Alan Pardew and the support from the Premier League right down to the National League, there has been no end of messages I have had, which is comforting.

‘That first Saturday after being out, I didn’t want to be watching or listening to the game, I just wanted to get away because that is the worst. I have had two clubs ring me, there are ongoing conversations and I am just making sure it is the right vehicle for me. What I mean by that is I want an owner that is aligned and who thinks they can compete to get out of their league.

‘My record speaks for itself. If you ask most managers how many promotions and trophies they have won, I bet over long careers, they haven’t got many. For me, with the smallest budget in the leagues, we maximised the team and maximised success.

‘To get two promotions and an FA Trophy win against Wrexham, hitting the play-offs four times in five years, that is something I am really proud of. If nothing else, the Bromley supporters and town are grateful.’

#1282. 2026/27 Premier League Table Without 'VAR Errors'

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

Video Assistant Referee (VAR) has its fair share of critics. Introduced to the Premier League at the start of the 2019/20 season, the technology was designed to help the on-pitch officials and ensure matches were officiated seamlessly and without controversy.

However, it has not had the impact that it was intended to have. If anything, the number of refereeing controversies has gone up, and many high-profile names, including Roy Keane and Wayne Rooney, have lost patience and want to see VAR scrapped.

But what would the 2026/27 Premier League table look like if every refereeing decision was correct? After every matchday in England's top tier, Squawka asks their followers to vote on controversial VAR decisions and whether the right decision was made or not.

Using that data, they have created a Premier League table without VAR errors following matchday 10, and it makes for interesting reading.

The table has been compiled on the basis that penalties, should they have been awarded, would have been converted.

Sunderland have had a dismal start to the campaign. The Black Cats, who are competing in the Conference League after finishing seventh in 2025/26, are currently rock bottom of the Premier League, having picked up five points from their opening ten games. They can't blame VAR for their troubles, either, as they would remain in the same position without its errors.

Crystal Palace would be second bottom, with Manchester United rounding out the relegation places. Nottingham Forest, who are currently 16th in the Premier League, would be two points better off and would be up in 14th, above Palace and United in the table, had VAR been perfect.

Back in September, Forest and Tottenham Hotspur drew 0-0 at the City Ground. VAR is adjudged to have wrongly intervened to disallow Neco Williams' goal for the home side. The Premier League released a statement explaining the goal had been ruled out for handball, but many felt the footage was inconclusive and not clear and obvious. Had VAR made the right decision, Forest would have won 1-0.

Coventry City currently sit 17th in the table, as is correct for them. But Fulham actually find themselves one place higher than they should be, as a result of Forest's issues.

Hull City have had a tremendous start and currently sit 13th in the table, but they would be a point and two places worse off without VAR errors.

Tottenham Hotspur would find themselves two places worse off down in 13th if VAR decisions were correct, while Ipswich Town would be two places and two points better off up in 12th. Newcastle United currently find themselves in 12th in the table, but the Magpies would be up in 11th with an extra point and a +6 goal difference swing in their favour.

Premier League Table Without VAR Errors (20-11)

Aston Villa are currently the team propping up the top half of the table with 13 points and a -3 goal difference from their opening ten games. But while their league position wouldn't have changed, the VAR decisions being correct would have them two points better off.

Leeds have had a strong start to the season, but they would be one point worse off in ninth in the table without any VAR errors, while Bournemouth would be dropping down to 8th in the table, with a -1 swing in their goal difference.

Everton would find themselves in 7th in the table, one place worse off, although they would still have 16 points and a +2 goal difference. Brentford are the biggest losers in the top half of the table, as they would be two places better off up in 6th place with two more points.

While the top five would be unchanged in terms of their standings, the points totals would be widely different. Chelsea and Liverpool currently sit fifth and fourth in the Premier League table with 16 and 18 points respectively, but with VAR errors being corrected, both teams should be on 19 points.

Manchester City would be two points worse off in third place, also on 19 points if VAR errors were fixed. They won 1-0 at Old Trafford thanks to Erling Haaland's winner. ProRef released a statement revealing that the goal should have been ruled out due to Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position. Without that goal, the match would've ended in a goalless draw.

Brighton would still be second place on 22 points with a +19 goal difference, but they should be two points closer to league leaders Arsenal.

Arsenal have picked up 27 points from their opening nine matches, winning nine and losing one. They wouldn't have beaten Liverpool without VAR errors, though.

Liverpool felt aggrieved that they weren't given a penalty when Alexander Isak's shirt was tugged by Jurrien Timber in the box, preventing him from having a header at goal. If VAR had made the right decision, Liverpool would've been given a spot-kick, and it is assumed they would have scored and that the spoils would have been shared.

Despite that, Mikel Arteta's side would still be well clear at the top of the table without VAR errors.

Premier League Table Without VAR Errors (10-1)

#1279. Crystal Palace will sack Pierre Sage after disastrous 16-game spell - this is how his reign fell apart over late, intense sessions, dinner at the training ground and an unpopular assistant manager

Published: 10:17 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:58 EST, 11 November 2026

Crystal Palace players and club chiefs have grown frustrated over Pierre Sage's training methods, Daily Mail Sport can reveal - and the 47-year-old will be sacked having won just two of his first ten Premier League matches.

A 3-1 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday saw Palace drop to bottom of the Premier League for the first time in nine years and proved to be the final straw for club bosses, who will tell the Frenchman his time is up.

Daily Mail Sport understands that while the Palace players got on well with Sage, they were frustrated by his late training sessions – with some not starting until 4pm. The regimented routine required players to stay at the training ground for dinner on the night before matches, with some not returning home until 8pm ahead of a 2pm kick-off the following day.

The club's hierarchy, meanwhile, expressed concerns early in the Frenchman's tenure that he was not doing enough defensive work on the training pitch.

Sage's philosophy was that the best way to defend was having the ball, meaning training sessions focused on running, pressing and possession rather than defensive structure.

But the lack of focus led to a poor defensive record, with Palace conceding 30 goals in 16 matches across all competitions. Defending set-pieces and counter-attacks has been a persistent problem for Sage’s side.

Pierre Sage will become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season after a dismal spell at Crystal Palace

Palace sit rock bottom of the Premier League after winning just two of their first 10 games

Daily Mail Sport understands many players voiced fears they were being pushed too hard in training, with sessions the day before a game particularly intense. There were also significant concerns about the quality of Sage's backroom staff, with his assistant Jamal Alioui proving especially unpopular among the players.

There has also been considerable turnover among senior executives, with six departures over the past 18 months. Chief financial officer Mitesh Velani is set to add to that number in the coming months. One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that the disruption to the club’s business operations has the hallmarks of a club heading for relegation.

As Palace look to bail themselves out of trouble, Daily Mail Sport understands former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank is in pole position to replace Sage, with six-pointers against Hull City and Coventry City following the international break. Sean Dyche also has admirers at Selhurst Park.

Palace chairman Steve Parish first contemplated sacking Sage over his lack of defensive nous in September, but gave him a stay of execution after Palace kept a clean sheet in a spirited performance away at Leeds on the eve of the international break. However, that display proved an anomaly as Palace shipped 19 goals in the following nine games.

Palace have won just once in their last eight matches in all competitions, beating Fulham 1-0 in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

In September, Daily Mail Sport revealed tensions had emerged between Sage and Parish when the latter took a dim view of the decision to drop teenage defender Jaydee Canvot in their defeat by Ipswich Town.

Palace paid French club RC Lens £4million in compensation to appoint Sage in June after he won the French Cup, finished second in Ligue 1 behind Paris Saint-Germain and was named manager of the season last term. It was the first time in 10 years that Palace had paid compensation to appoint a manager.

Palace chairman Steve Parish (right) first contemplated dismissing Sage in September over a lack of defensive nous

Palace players found Sage’s training sessions too intense and struggled to adapt to the late schedule

Succeeding Oliver Glasner, Palace's greatest manager, proved too big a task for the 47-year-old.

Following Palace's loss to Liverpool, Sage insisted the Eagles have been playing better than their league position suggests and pleaded for more time.

'A lot of times I’ve said we deserved better and it was the case again (on Sunday),' said Sage. 'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

‘I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in (me), and if it's not the case, they will take a decision. I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100 per cent involved in what I have to do.

‘We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be OK.’

#1278. ‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Ursula Martin is an emeritus professor at the Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford, UK.

In early October, the artificial-intelligence firm OpenAI posted more than 700 AI-generated mathematical manuscripts on an online public repository. The arguments — if found to be correct after verification — contain an extraordinary trove of new mathematical knowledge. The reaction to these developments from the maths community has ranged from exhilaration to despair. Some researchers worry they have spent their lifetimes attempting to solve problems and their work might now suddenly seem meaningless. Others have expressed concern about the negative impact on young colleagues who are entering the field during a period of flux. And there’s been widespread anger at the manner in which AI companies are releasing such findings.

As one of the authors of the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics, which was published in June, I think some of the field’s concerns over OpenAI’s approach to announcing its discoveries could have been anticipated. In our declaration, we did not oppose the use of AI but put forwards several practical safeguards. These included the need for clear citation policies, precise disclosures on how AI is used and a renewed commitment to the long-standing expectation that all arguments made in a maths proof should be independently verifiable and answerable by a human author. Some AI companies have agreed to follow the declaration. OpenAI has not.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow

Now that mathematicians have started analysing the AI-assisted proofs, it’s clear that many of the 700 preprints are presented in a sloppy, rough-and-ready style, making them hard to understand. The inner workings of OpenAI’s closed models are unknown, and there is also no human author named who might take responsibility for explaining or correcting the content if flaws emerge. It will take mathematicians a lot of time and effort to check the work in the preprints and rewrite it in a professional format that is suitable for judgement by peer reviewers. Unsurprisingly, many mathematicians are unenthusiastic about clearing up OpenAI’s mess, however exciting the underlying mathematics might be.

So, what does this mean for the future of mathematics? Creatively rethinking how the field must evolve will require action at every level. Outstanding leadership by individuals such as mathematician Terence Tao, and grassroots initiatives such as the Leiden declaration, need to be complemented with high-level engagement from stakeholder institutions such as the International Mathematical Union. It would be a disservice to the field if AI companies are allowed to set the norms on how to do mathematics without wide-ranging input from academics.

Manchester United are currently finalising a deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager to replace Michael Carrick, GIVEMESPORT understands.

Pochettino, who is currently in charge of the USMNT, has a £7.4m exit clause in his contract with US Soccer, and GMS understands that it will cost a further £1.5m for him to bring his backroom staff with him too. But a deal is now close to being finalised, with Carrick expected to be relieved of his duties in the coming days.

Pochettino has previously had spells at three different Premier League clubs, having shone during a spell with Southampton, before taking over at Tottenham Hotspur and leading them to a second-place finish in the top flight, while he also reached the EFL Cup final and Champions League final with the north London side.

A brief spell with Paris Saint-Germain followed, where he won the Ligue 1 title, before he returned to London to coach Chelsea. At Stamford Bridge, he led the team to a fourth-place finish while he also reached the EFL Cup final again, losing in extra-time to Liverpool.

But despite a relatively successful season with the Blues, Pochettino was sacked after just one season with the club.

Pochettino's time at Chelsea is best remembered for the form and performances of Cole Palmer under his management, and Man Utd fans will be hopeful that he can get similar performances out of a number of stars at Old Trafford.

The poor campaign this season has been well noted, and many have blamed the poor running stats of Carrick's team. United have ranked second bottom of the entire division for distance covered and distance covered per 90 minutes, behind only Liverpool.

"That's [ball work] what it's been like mostly," he said on Rio Ferdinand Presents.

"Not loads of running?" Ferdinand queried.

"When you come back from the World Cup, you don't do loads of running. Just chill."

But speaking after Pochettino's exit at Chelsea, midfield general Moises Caicedo commented on the tactics he would employ, and noted that they relied heavily on running and fitness to be successful.

"At Brighton, it was all tactical, just with the ball; tactical, tactical, tactical. And at Chelsea, it was run, run, run and it was very difficult for me. With Chelsea, I always ran a bit more, and with Brighton we almost always had the ball, with Chelsea it was a different football, and we had to run more."

Pochettino's first game in charge of Man Utd, barring any unexpected changes, is expected to be against old rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22nd.

Lazio could also face another transfer block in January. If it’s confirmed, they wouldn’t be able to raise their wage bill, so renewals would have to be on the same or lower terms.

Isaksen’s deal runs until 2028, and Lazio are ready to reward his best spell since joining the club. The Danish winger has scored four goals in his last six games, and he could see his salary rise from €1.5m to around €2.5m net a season. He’s reportedly keen to commit his long-term future to the club.

There’s less urgency with Nicolò Rovella. He has made only 12 appearances in 2026, totalling just over 600 minutes, and neither side is in a rush, although a decision will be needed by the end of the season. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru’s future also needs to be resolved.

Mattia Cataldi, Manuel Lazzari, Matteo Cancellieri and Luca Pellegrini all have contracts expiring in 2027 and could leave next summer. Josip Šutalo, Davide Frattesi and Albert Gudmundsson are on loan.

#1275. Some Man Utd Stars Wanted Unai Emery Instead of Mauricio Pochettino

A number of Manchester United players were hoping the club would appoint Unai Emery as their new head coach, according to a report.

United are expected to sack Michael Carrick following a dismal start to the season, according to GIVEMESPORT sources. Indeed, the Reds sit 18th in the Premier League table after winning just ONE of their opening 10 top-flight matches.

Carrick reported to training on Wednesday, but a decision has been made on his future with United expected to hold a meeting to inform the 45-year-old that he has been relieved of his duties.

With Carrick facing the axe, United are poised to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. It's believed the Reds are now finalising a move for the United States national team manager with an agreement in principle reached on personal terms.

Pochettino's USMNT contract contains a £7.5million release clause, though his backroom staff are expected to increase the overall cost of hire. The Argentine's current deal is set to expire in 2030, after the next World Cup.

With most of United's first-team players out on international duty with their respective countries, the squad anticipates that Pochettino will be their new head coach when they return.

However, according to talkSPORT, some United players were hoping for the appointment of Aston Villa boss Emery instead.

Emery, who was in the dugout for Villa's dramatic 4-4 draw against Carrick's United on Sunday, is in talks with the Villans over a new and improved contract, having done a superb job in the West Midlands.

The Spaniard took charge of Villa back in October 2022, following the dismissal of Steven Gerrard, and has since spearheaded the club back to the Champions League twice in three years and guided them to their first trophy in 25 years.

As for Carrick, he is yet to be given any clarity over his future. United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox recommended a change of manager during a meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS in Monaco on Tuesday, but that decision hasn't been communicated to Carrick, who has been left in the dark.

Hansi Flick was certainly full of praise for Emery earlier this season, ahead of Barcelona hosting Villa in the Champions League.

It will also be difficult because they are managed by Unai Emery. He is one of the best coaches in Europe and the world.

"You look at his team, and they have a clear structure in both defence and attack. They have different patterns of play and are very dangerous."

United are on a run of just one win in 10 matches across all competitions, and that came in the 3-2 comeback success against Roma last Tuesday. Before that included damaging losses against Chelsea, Bournemouth and Como.

Should Pochettino be appointed, as expected, his first game in charge is set to be a daunting-looking trip to Anfield to face Liverpool after the November international break. That is followed by another away game, this time at Sporting CP in the Champions League.

#1274. Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of biggest shocks in League Cup history

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

“You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”

This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”.

A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM

The precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

So while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

It was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

Salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Eberechi Eze are among the players stepping off the bus, so at the very least it will be a strong bench.

Aside from their stadium being called Highbury, Fleetwood Town’s red shirts with white sleeves also bear a striking resemblance to Arsenal’s home kit. The club in its current guise was founded in 1997, although previous iterations date back to 1908 under the name Fleetwood FC.

There is no evidence or anecdote suggesting Arsenal were the inspiration, so it appears the kit clash is a coincidence. Arsenal will be wearing their navy away strip.

The club’s most famous son is surely Jamie Vardy, who scored 31 goals in 36 appearances for Fleetwood in the 2011-12 season before Leicester City made their move.

An unfamiliar opponent at a very familiar sounding venue, Arsenal play Fleetwood Town for the first time this evening at the Lancashire club’s Highbury Stadium.

Fleetwood, 18th in League Two, are the lowest-ranked team remaining in this season’s League Cup, having booked their place in the fourth round thanks to a victory at Sheffield United.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

Max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

Matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Arteta said: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”Full team news on the way shortly.

#1273. Taking instructions from a schoolboy and showing class at half-pace... William Saliba made impressive injury comeback for Arsenal Under-21s - now he faces fight to take Ezri Konsa's spot, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 06:24 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:28 EST, 11 November 2026

It was a scene straight out of Will Ferrell's Elf. In the middle of Arsenal's Under-21 team huddle stood William Saliba, all 6ft 4in of him, towering over his teenage team-mates as 17-year-old captain Marli Salmon delivered his pre-match rallying cry.

One of the world's finest defenders was taking instructions from a schoolboy.

For the hundreds of Arsenal supporters who had descended on Boreham Wood's Meadow Park on Sunday, it was an extraordinary sight. Four months after suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat by Spain, Saliba was finally back on a football pitch.

But his carefully managed 45-minute appearance in a 5-2 victory over Aston Villa's Under-21s marked the beginning of another challenge. Saliba must now win back a place in an Arsenal defence which, remarkably, has barely missed him.

That is largely down to Ezri Konsa, the £55million summer signing from Aston Villa who has been so impressive in Saliba's absence that Mikel Arteta faces a genuine selection dilemma.

Saliba and Gabriel have been Arsenal's established central defensive partnership since the opening day of the 2022-23 season. But Konsa, arguably Arsenal's outstanding defender this term, has made a compelling case to keep his place.

William Saliba towered over his teenage team-mates and played 45 minutes on Sunday

His performance in the 1-0 victory at Liverpool, Arsenal's first win at Anfield in 14 years, was particularly impressive. He won every ground duel, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances, leading the match statistics in all three categories. Liverpool failed to register a shot on target.

It was precisely the sort of performance that has given Arteta something to think about. And the Arsenal manager is understood to have challenged Konsa to fight for his place rather than simply make way for the returning Frenchman.

There is another solution. Konsa can operate at right back, a position he has occupied for both Villa and England, including during the summer's World Cup. That would allow Arteta to restore the Saliba-Gabriel partnership without sacrificing a player who has become such an important part of Arsenal's defence. For now, however, there will be no rush.

Saliba's injury history explains why Arsenal have been so careful. In 2022-23, another back problem kept him out for 97 days and contributed significantly to the collapse of a title challenge that had seen the club spend 248 days at the top of the Premier League.

Arsenal have since finished runners-up again and finally claimed the title last summer, but the lessons of that earlier setback have not been forgotten.

Leading back specialists were consulted over Saliba's latest injury before the club settled on a conservative rehabilitation programme, deliberately extending his recovery rather than risking another setback.

He returned to full first-team training last Tuesday, ahead of Arsenal's 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague, but Sunday's appearance represented his first competitive action since July. His absence from France's squad during the international break should allow Arsenal to continue building his fitness without interruption.

And there was plenty to suggest that the long wait has done little to diminish his quality.

The Frenchman is building up his fitness after four months on the sidelines

Saliba faces a tough test to try and break up the partnership formed by Gabriel and Ezri Konsa

Playing comfortably within himself, Saliba repeatedly strolled past opponents before threading passes through the Villa midfield. At times he ventured so far forward after set-pieces that supporters began joking about whether he fancied himself as a centre-forward.

Even at half-pace, the gulf between a world-class defender and academy football was obvious.

Yet it was Saliba's interaction with his young team-mates that provided some of the afternoon's most revealing moments.

Throughout the first half he could be heard directing Salmon, shouting 'man on,' 'high, high' and 'well done, Marli' as he guided his teenage defensive partner through the game.

When Arsenal scored their opening goal, Salmon initially stayed back rather than joining the celebrations. Saliba promptly ordered him forward to enjoy the moment.

Marli Salmon, pictured laying a wreath for Remembrance Day, was the one barking out instructions and seeing Saliba (left) among the youngsters was an extraordinary sight

It was a small gesture but typical of the interest Saliba has taken in Arsenal's younger players during his rehabilitation.

He is understood to have spent time asking about their families and offering advice about life in professional football.

One particular message has been the importance of looking after their parents if they are fortunate enough to make a successful career in the game. The affection is clearly mutual.

Children clamoured for autographs as Saliba arrived and departed, while Arsenal had prepared for the unusual attention surrounding an Under 21 fixture.

Large QR codes directing spectators to the team line-up had been displayed around the ground and a member of the first-team security staff accompanied Saliba between the dressing room and the pitch.

His afternoon was meticulously choreographed. At half-time, his work completed, he disappeared into the changing rooms before leaving through a side exit.

Saliba made his comeback for Arsenal's Under 21 side after a long injury absence

The 45 minutes will have provided reassurance to Arteta and Arsenal's medical staff, as well as a memorable afternoon for the teenagers who shared the pitch with him. For Saliba, though, the real work is only beginning.

Few would have imagined when he suffered his injury in July that he might return to find his place under threat. Konsa's performances have changed that calculation.

Arsenal have their defensive cornerstone back. Now Arteta must decide what to do with him.

#1272. Man Utd ‘Up For Sale’ as Financial Expert Reveals the Glazers’ Asking Price

Manchester United fans remain disgruntled with the current ownership of the club, with another manager on the verge of the sack.

Michael Carrick is set to become the seventh permanent manager to be shown the exit door since Sir Alex Ferguson's reign ended in 2013.

However, many within the fan base are adamant that the real problem at Old Trafford is the hierarchy, and until that is in order, any manager will struggle to get the English giants back to the top of European football.

Protests took place inside the ground during United's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday. Green and gold balloons were deployed along with a banner, which read: "We don't want a new stadium, we want the owners out."

The Glazer family have been major shareholders in the club since Malcolm Glazer assumed full control in May 2005. They have been far from popular figures in Manchester, with debt mounting ever since they arrived.

Speaking to talkSPORT, financial expert Stefan Borson revealed that United fans hoping for the Glazers to sell could get their wish in the near future.

Michael Carrick is set to be sacked as Manchester United's head coach with Mauricio Pochettino in line to replace him at Old Trafford

Borson stated: "My understanding from somebody, a senior person in the game, told me that there is a process and that they are for sale.

"You would question why they wouldn't make it public, although when they last made a process public, that of course ended with a slightly disappointing outcome (Ratcliffe's shares)."

He went on to claim that the Glazers hadn't made their intentions public, which could be linked to the fallout from Sir Jim Ratcliffe's arrival in 2024. "They may be trying something different by not making it formal, but they are now accepting that now is the time," he said.

"They (Glazers) are robust, and they will only go when their price is met.

"They believe this is a club that has such a robust brand that even if they are unsuccessful on the pitch, it has very little difference to the commercial viability and ability to generate revenue."

Borson expects the asking price to be in the region of £5 billion, citing FSG's deal to sell 38% of Liverpool to the 1892 Holdings Consortium as a yardstick.

#1270. Pochettino Can Lead New Era at Man Utd With Move for Cole Palmer to Replace Bruno Fernandes

Manchester United are set to enter a new era at Old Trafford, as they close in on the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils are expected to sack manager Michael Carrick this week after he led the team to just one win in 10 Premier League games so far this season, leaving the team 18th in the table heading into the international break.

GIVEMESPORT sources understand that United chiefs have reached an agreement on personal terms with Pochettino, with the contract he signed with the USMNT in the summer to continue as their manager until 2030 containing a $10m (£7.4m) release clause. The Argentine is keen to take over at Old Trafford.

Should he sign on the dotted line to be the man in the dugout, Pochettino will have some major issues to sort out. A number of defensive signings are needed in 2027, with INEOS reportedly planning a rebuild in the summer.

That leads on from Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw all being out of contract at the end of the current season, while there are doubts about the long-term futures of Noussair Mazraoui, Matthijs De Ligt, and Diogo Dalot, who was booed off by fans in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend.

There is also a need to bolster the attack. Joshua Zirkzee's future looks bleak, Marcus Rashford will be entering the final year of his contract, Amad hasn't scored a goal in almost a full calendar year, and Bruno Fernandes' contract is set to expire, with talks over an extension having stalled.

A Bruno exit is not something the club will be hoping for, but it is certainly more possible now than it was a few months ago. There is said to be interest from a number of clubs in Europe and in Saudi Arabia, while the player himself could be tempted considering his age.

Should he move on, then replacing his goals and assists would immediately need to become a priority for the recruitment department. Players like Nico Paz and Morgan Gibbs-White have been linked with stepping up to the plate, but the strongest link has come in the shape of Chelsea sensation Cole Palmer.

The former Man City academy star grew up as a Man Utd fan and was understood to be open to making the move to Old Trafford last summer, before Fernandes committed his future to United, and he then signed a new extension at Stamford Bridge.

But it was Pochettino who took Palmer to Stamford Bridge and coached him to become one of the franchise players in the division, and a reunion could be something beneficial to both players.

Since moving to Chelsea, Palmer has thrived as the main man at the heart of everything. Much like Bruno, he is the focal point of every attack. But he has some attributes that Fernandes doesn't have, which make him a better fit in the modern game.

Palmer is a far better dribbler and is capable of beating players one-on-one, while he is also capable of getting goals and assists when playing in a wider position. That would allow for more tactical flexibility depending on match situations or availability.

He's also just 24 years old, meaning he still has the best part of a decade to go in his career, when he could be playing at the very highest level. Fernandes, meanwhile, is on the way down, as his performances this season have shown.

Any deal would obviously be incredibly difficult to do. Chelsea won't want to sell their best player, and especially not to a direct rival. But with the player's buy-in, it's possible. INEOS could make a major statement by bringing him in, filling an instant hole in the squad, and upgrading.

Pochettino would be getting a player he knows well and can get the best out of, and together they can lead a new era at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino is a leading contender to take over as Man Utd manager, and he already has his own Dele Alli at Old Trafford.

#1269. These AI agents design your perfect robot-powered lab — and run it for you

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Artificial-intelligence agents can devise a detailed procedure for a robotic arm and test it in a virtual laboratory.Credit: Jiaru Bai & Yuchi Zhao, University of Toronto

Laboratory robots are tireless and uncomplaining, but they have narrow skill sets, limited mobility and an inability to get out of each other’s way. Now, a system of artificial-intelligence agents promises to help lab robots do their best work.

In this process, a scientist describes their research programme and lab set-up to the agents, which then create step-by-step experimental protocols for the lab’s robots. The agents also generate a virtual version of the lab and test the protocols there. They can then direct the robots in the real lab to perform the research.

Robot chemist sparks row with claim it created new materials

Robot chemist sparks row with claim it created new materials

The agents can even design an entire lab from scratch, using a virtual one to work out the ideal placement for instruments and robots.

The system is described in a preprint posted in October to arXiv1. It has not been peer reviewed.

In a test, the agents wrote more than 200 commands directing a robotic arm to move between and interact with instruments in an existing lab space. The agent simulated the steps in the virtual lab to ensure that it all worked smoothly, then directed the real-life arm to carry out procedures to measure the optical properties of nanocrystals.

The concept is “very cool” and could drastically reduce the effort required to set up automated labs, says Evan Collins, a bioengineer at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge. But integrating the cameras and sensors that the agents need to direct experiments effectively could require more resources than does setting up a lab manually, he says.

The simulations would make it easy to plan robotic movements that avoid collisions between robots and other objects in the lab, says Collins.

This could ease the process of getting labs up and running, given that setting up an automated lab is often a time-consuming process of trial and error followed by extensive testing and troubleshooting. Because the agents conduct all the planning and testing in a simulated environment, there is no need for researchers to “babysit the system” after it’s built, says Yuchi (Allan) Zhao, a roboticist at the University of Toronto in Canada and co-author of the preprint.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03587-x

The game between Manchester City and Brighton at The Etihad has ended 2-2, therefore it has now gone to penalties.

Gusto’s behaviour in recent minutes has been appalling. First he went down after virtually no contact from Van Dijk and now goes down again, once more not a foul. Andoni Iraola is turning to his bench for the first time tonight and makes a double substitution as Wirtz and Barcola replace McConnell and Koumas. Some double change that for Liverpool!

It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike remain long-term absentees for the hosts with Jeremie Frimpong also missing. Florian Wirtz could feature despite going off with an ankle knock during the win over Brighton.

Like Liverpool, Chelsea also had an all-Premier League tie in the third round of this competition, beating Leeds 6-3 in a high-scoring affair at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea come into tonight’s game off the back of a 2-0 defeat against Tottenham in the league last weekend. Not only did they lose on Saturday but to make matters worse for them Cole Palmer was sent off. As a result of that red card, Palmer is suspended for tonight’s tie.

“We [Alonso and Palmer] spoke and for sure he knows the mistake he made,” Alonso said. “Things that you can avoid. I hope that this is not going to be repeated. He is aware of that, he is mature and it was a mistake. He is in a good space, he connects very well socially with his teammates. They like him, they want Cole smiling, they want Cole having fun, enjoying his game because when we see that, he will have a better team. I will just ask you because he has got this very cool persona, you probably know his personality is very interesting.”

Former Liverpool midfielder and current Chelsea boss Alonso has lost his two games as a manager against Liverpool; a 4-0 defeat as Bayer Leverkusen boss and then a 1-0 loss when in charge of Real Madrid, with both taking place at Anfield. Alonso is not the only ex-Liverpool midfielder to return to Anfield tonight as their former captain Jordan Henderson is in the Chelsea squad for tonight. Joao Pedro has missed the trip to Anfield because of a thigh injury which could rule him out for a few weeks.

The Premier league fixture between these sides at Anfield ended in a 1-1 draw back in May. In that match, Arne Slot was in charge of Liverpool with Calum McFarlane in interim charge of Chelsea. Chelsea won the reverse fixture 2-1 at Stamford Bridge. Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1267. Como sporting director Ludi: ‘Business with Real Madrid adds value to our football’

Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi says the club’s close ties with Real Madrid are good for Italian football as a whole, and he has confirmed that Jacobo Ramón will stay at the club for the rest of the season.

According to the Corriere dello Sport, the Lariani’s relationship with Real Madrid has been one of the keys to their rise. They have brought in Nico Paz and Ramón from the Spanish giants, and Roma are now trying to sign Endrick from them.

“We have a great relationship with them,” Ludi said. “The basis isn’t so much the relationship with Real itself, but the valuable relationships we’ve built, both with prestigious clubs and within our own club. We take care of relationships. It isn’t something you can take for granted.

“The Nico Paz deal was a win-win situation. We had the chance to invest in a player with great potential, and they believed in our technical project, thanks partly to Fàbregas’ credibility and ability.

“I’ve never commented on other clubs’ deals, but it’s significant that talent can be brought to Italy. Como are an example of how young players can help you achieve very important results. This year, young players have a much higher share of minutes than in recent seasons, and that’s a very good sign for Serie A.”

Ramón received his first Spain call-up this week, but Ludi says the defender isn’t going anywhere for now.

“When we went to negotiate for Nico Paz, there was an update on his position, and he’ll definitely stay with us for the whole season. It’s still too early to know what his future might hold.”

Como aren’t planning any major signings in January. Instead, they’re waiting for Moise Kean, Assane Diao and Jesús Rodríguez to return from injury.

“We may look at outgoing deals for players who aren’t getting much game time. In terms of signings, we don’t have anything incredible planned. We’re very happy with the squad. If an opportunity came up and we needed small improvements, we could act, but I’d mainly back the players we already have.”

Ludi also highlighted Como’s commitment to Italian youngsters. Riccardo Cassano has earned an Italy call-up, and Papaccioli scored in the Champions League.

Sunday’s defeat at San Siro left Fàbregas’ side six points behind Inter, but Ludi was full of praise for the champions.

“We’ve had an extraordinary start to the season. Our challenge was to stay competitive while playing every three days, and our Champions League run shows we’ve managed that. Inter are the strongest team in Italy, and they approached the game extraordinarily well. We need to improve and grow. I’m sure we’ll learn from that game too.”
